scope: Retrospective offline article benchmark, normal-only training, full eligible SBI-request test sets, no attack generation or replay
split: Chronological whole-timestamp boundaries, first 40% normal for training, next 10% calibration, remaining 50% clean holdout. Every mixed/attack capture is evaluated in full, including unknown rows in predictions but excluding them from labelled metrics. No test sampling or size cap. Each partition resets its causal history; no windows share events across partitions.
primary_metric: Average precision (stepwise PR area) and recall at frozen calibration FPR 0.1%, with actual test FPR, not test-tuned thresholds
training_objective: All methods train only on original normal events. Four existing architectures and published Granomaly TGN use identical benign-edge versus independently permuted endpoint negative sampling. Synthetic negatives never enter histories or graphs. Sequence negatives replace only the current token, retaining a real normal-only past. Deep SVDD, KitNET and Isolation Forest fit the same normal feature vectors.
evaluation_state: Weights fixed. Graph models reset, replay normal training history, then score each evaluation batch before blindly observing that batch. No evaluation labels enter memory. Sequence windows are bounded and causal. Native Granomaly memory update at evaluation is an explicitly disclosed common-protocol adaptation.
features: Training-only endpoint vocabulary with one unknown bucket; fixed-hash method/service/resource representations, wire version, causal gaps and past traffic counts. Context adds past operation representations and caller-history diversity. No binary novelty-rule outputs. All eight methods receive each of the same two feature compositions.

granomaly_reference.adaptations: Unchanged published neural modules (100-d memory/time/embedding, 2-head TransformerConv), common features, 12 fixed epochs, 512-event batches, 50 neighbors, training-only node vocabulary, common label-blind evaluation updates and normal-calibrated thresholds. This is an adapted direct comparison, not a claim to reproduce published numerical results.

kitnet_reference.adaptations: Published KitNET algorithm on common SBI features rather than full Kitsune packet-statistics pipeline; max AE size 10, feature mapping first 20% of training, remaining normal training for AE updates, execute-only calibration/test. np.Inf alias supplied for NumPy 2 compatibility, no algorithm edits. Author-fixed seed 1234: one deterministic fit, not three independent repeats.

deep_svdd_reference.adaptations: Equation (4) one-class objective, tabular bias-free input-64-32-16 ReLU network, fixed initial-mean center clipped away from zero by 0.1, 12 epochs, Adam weight decay. Independent implementation, not authors' image-network code.

isolation_forest_reference.implementation: scikit-learn 1.6.1 IsolationForest, 200 trees, max_samples=256 by algorithm design, every normal training row supplied; all test rows scored

uncertainty: Three initialization seeds are not independent deployments. Conditional within-record moving-block bootstrap (512 requests, 200 replicates) for confusion metrics; no population-of-deployments confidence claim. Dataset-specific results remain separate.
release: Only deidentified numeric feature matrices, anonymous node/episode indices, labels, score arrays, aggregate reports and hashes; no raw PCAP, tokens, raw requests or address vocabularies
limitations: Both datasets and some coverage statistics were already inspected: evaluation is retrospective, not a newly untouched prospective test
CTD5G has one mixed collection; all observed positive SBI requests use previously unseen edges
Marker-associated positive labels do not independently verify malicious impact
No CU/witness measurements available: this benchmark tests ML components, not the complete integrity-monitoring method
Request rows, windows, initializations and repeated fits do not increase independent attack/deployment counts
Published baselines are rerun under a common protocol with all adaptations disclosed; numbers from unrelated papers are not directly ranked
